# @ratmath/analytic 0.1.0: full documentation

> Certified calculus on exact rationals: function values, ranges, integrals, zeros, extrema, limits, Taylor models and validated ODE steps, built on @ratmath/core. From https://ratmath.com/analytic/, commit b60afb3. Each page ends with a runnable example; in it, PRINT(...) prints.


---

Page: https://ratmath.com/analytic/index.html

@ratmath/analytic

## Answers about functions that come with a proof

A JavaScript library for calculus on exact rational numbers. Ask for a value, a range, an integral, the zeros or the solution of a differential equation. You get a floating-point answer at once, then an interval that is guaranteed to contain the true answer.

Move the slider. The curve and the guesses follow at float speed. When you stop, the zeros are proven, each one in its own small bracket that is shown to contain exactly one. The integral and the range come back as intervals, and the true values are inside them.

### Why intervals

Most values of `exp`, `sin` or an integral are irrational, so no fraction is exactly right. RatMath's answer is a rational interval that certainly contains the true value, as narrow as you ask. Every step that could lose accuracy (a truncated series, a rounded constant, a range over a whole interval) is counted and added to the interval. So the result is a statement you can rely on, not an estimate.

Underneath sits the [Taylor model](https://ratmath.com/analytic/models.html): an exact polynomial plus an interval remainder, valid on a whole interval of inputs. Arithmetic, composition, integration and ODE steps all act on these models and keep that guarantee.

### A first program

```js
import { R } from "@ratmath/core";
import { fn, zeros, ode } from "@ratmath/analytic";

const f = fn("exp(sin(x))*x");
f.value("1/3").quick.value;          // 0.46235716975704894 (float, at once)
f.value("1/3", { digits: 30 }).exact();  // RationalInterval, 30 correct digits
f.integral(0, 1).exact();            // certified ∫₀¹
f.derivative().toString();           // "exp(sin(x))*cos(x)*x + exp(sin(x))"

zeros("x^3 - 3x + 1", [-3, 3]).exact();   // three brackets, each with exactly one zero
ode.solve({ f: "y^2 + t", y0: "1/2", until: "1/2" }).exact().final;  // y(1/2), certified
```

### Topics

- [Explore](https://ratmath.com/analytic/explore.html): Type any function and ask questions

- [Fast, then certified](https://ratmath.com/analytic/fast.html): Previews, progress, sliders

- [Taylor models](https://ratmath.com/analytic/models.html): Polynomial plus remainder

- [Many digits](https://ratmath.com/analytic/values.html): exp, log, sin, π with error bounds

- [Formulas](https://ratmath.com/analytic/expressions.html): Parsing and symbolic d/dx

- [Ranges and integrals](https://ratmath.com/analytic/ranges.html): Bernstein bounds, adaptive pieces

- [Zeros and extrema](https://ratmath.com/analytic/zeros.html): Sturm, Krawczyk, multiplicity

- [Piecewise](https://ratmath.com/analytic/piecewise.html): Regions like 2n :x:! 2n+1

- [ODEs](https://ratmath.com/analytic/odes.html): Validated Picard steps

- [Your own series](https://ratmath.com/analytic/series.html): Remainder rules you can check

### Try it

```js
const f = fn("exp(sin(x))*x");
PRINT("float preview:", f.value("1/3").quick.value);
PRINT("certified, 30 digits:", f.value("1/3", { digits: 30 }).exact());
PRINT("derivative:", f.derivative().toString());
PRINT("∫ from 0 to 1:", f.integral(0, 1, { digits: 10 }).exact());
PRINT("zeros of x^3 - 3x + 1:");
for (const z of zeros("x^3 - 3x + 1", [-3, 3]).exact()) PRINT("  ", z.kind, z.lo, "to", z.hi, z.unique ? "(exactly one)" : "");
ode.solve({ f: "y^2 + t", y0: "1/2", until: "1/2" }).exact().final
```

Page: https://ratmath.com/analytic/reference.html

Reference

## Everything in the library

Numbers can be JS integers, bigints, strings such as `"3/4"` or `"0.1"` (decimals are exact), Core `Rational`s, or Core intervals such as `R`1/2:1``. Functions marked R return a [Refinement](https://ratmath.com/analytic/fast.html): `.quick` is the float preview, `.exact()` or `await .settle()` gives the certified answer. When a hypothesis fails (a log of something that can reach 0, a divisor that can be 0, a point outside the domain), the library throws an `AnalyticError` with a `code` and a reason. It does not return a bound it cannot prove.

### Formulas

| call | returns | notes |

| fn(text, { variable, params }) | AnalyticFunction or PiecewiseFunction | Text, an AST, or the piecewise form "rule if region; …; rule otherwise" |

| f.value(x, { digits = 20, maxBits = 8192 }) | R RationalInterval | a point interval for rational-only formulas; bits double until the digits are met or maxBits is reached |

| f.range(I, { digits = 6, order = 8, maxPieces = 256 }) | R RationalInterval | preview: 256 samples (trust rough) |

| f.integral(a, b, { digits = 12, order = 12, maxPieces }) | R RationalInterval | preview: Gauss–Legendre |

| f.limit(c, { digits = 20, side }) | RationalInterval or ±Infinity | c is a rational point, "inf" or "-inf"; side is "left" or "right". Throws no-limit where the two sides differ or the function keeps oscillating |

| f.asymptotic("inf" \| "-inf") | { exp, power, log, coefficient, oscillates, term } | the leading behaviour ekx·xp·log(x)m·(coefficient + a part that dies out) |

| f.improperIntegral(a, b, { digits = 10, singular }) | R RationalInterval, ±Infinity or NaN | an end at "inf" / "-inf" or where f is undefined; singular lists interior singular points. ±Infinity is a proven divergence; an integral that cannot be decided throws undecided |

| f.taylor(c, n = 6, { digits }) | RationalInterval[] | enclosures of f⁽ᵏ⁾(c)/k! for k = 0…n, n ≤ 16; exact points for rational values; removable quotients are divided as series |

| f.derivative() | a new function | symbolic and simplified |

| f.model(D, { order, bits, centre }) | TaylorModel | certified on the domain D |

| f.regular() | a function | the same function with holes of its rational summands cancelled; used by range and integral |

| f.float(x) | number | no guarantee |

| f.with({ a: "3/8" }) | a new function | other parameter values (sliders) |

| f.toString() | string | calculator notation that parses back |

Grammar: `+ - * / ^` (or `**`), parentheses, implicit products (`2x`, `3(x+1)`, `2sin(x)`), `-x^2 = -(x^2)`, `^` right-associative. Functions: `exp log ln log1p sqrt cbrt sin cos tan asin acos atan sinh cosh tanh erf erfc abs min max` (`arcsin arccos arctan` too), `sec csc cot sech csch coth asinh acosh atanh` (written out in the others as they are read), and the special functions `gamma lgamma digamma trigamma beta(a, b) besselJ(n, x) Si fresnelS fresnelC`; constants `pi e`. A name of three or more letters written against a parenthesis, such as `foo(x)`, is refused as an unknown function rather than read as a product. A power with an odd denominator, `x^(1/3)`, is the real root and is defined for negative x. Ranges and integrals may cross points where the function is not smooth (`abs`, `cbrt` at 0); there the bounds come from interval evaluation. It is the same grammar and the same plain AST as `@ratmath/graphics`.

### Features of a function

| call | record kinds | fields |

| zeros(f, [a, b], opts) | exact, sign-change, isolated, possible, undefined, everywhere | at, lo, hi, unique, multiplicity, atMost, bound, budget |

| poles(f, [a, b], opts) | pole, hole, undefined | order (rational poles), source: "log" (asymptotes of ln), value (a hole's limit) |

| extrema(f, [a, b], opts) | max, min, flat, possible, constant | value, unique, touching |

| inflections(f, [a, b], opts) | inflection, possible | value, unique, touching |

| simplestBetween(a, b) | Rational | smallest denominator in [a, b] |

All four are R. Options: `variable`, `params`, `tolerance` (bracket width, default 10⁻⁶), `pieces` (starting pieces, 16), `maxDepth` (48), `maxMultiplicity`, `flatBits`, `maxBoxes` (2000 per piece), `maxMs` (8000 in all), `sliceMs` (15). Previews are `{ kind: "guess", at }`. A stretch of the interval with no record certainly holds none.

| kind or field | meaning |

| exact | f(at) = 0 exactly, at a rational point |

| everywhere, constant | the function is identically zero (for zeros) or constant (for extrema) on [lo, hi]; one record covers the stretch |

| sign-change | f has opposite proven signs at lo and hi; with unique, exactly one zero inside |

| isolated | exactly one zero inside, but f keeps its sign (found through sqrt, abs or an even power) |

| possible | undecided: maybe no zero, maybe several; atMost: m bounds the count with multiplicity |

| undefined | f is not defined somewhere on the bracket |

| bound | proven max \|f\| on a possible bracket of a flat function |

| budget | the bracket was left when the work budget ran out |

| touching | f′ (or f″) has the same proven sign at both ends: no feature, or a pair of them inside |

### Piecewise

| call | returns | notes |

| piecewise([[region, rule], …], opts) | PiecewiseFunction | first matching piece wins |

| where`2:!x:8` | Region | template tag; values may be interpolated |

| new Region(text \| x => bool, { variable, params }) | Region | .test(x), .match(x) → { n }, .intervals(a, b), .breakpoints(a, b) |

| p.breaks([a, b]) | R records | { at, value, left, right, kind: continuous \| jump \| removable \| edge \| unproven, defined } |

| p.segments(a, b) | array | open pieces and points with the active rule |

| p.value, range, integral, zeros, extrema, inflections, poles, derivative | | piece by piece |

### Differential equations

| call | returns | notes |

| ode.solve({ f, y0, t0, until, order = 10, step, tol, maxSteps, vars, time, params, float }) | R ODESolution | preview: RK4 samples { t, y } |

| sol.at(t), sol.final, sol.steps, sol.complete, sol.reason, sol.describe() | | enclosures of y(t) |

| ode.step({ f, y0, step, order }) | { t0, t1, models, model } | one validated step, or an error |

`f` is a formula in `t` and `y`, an array of formulas for a system (`vars` names the unknowns), or a JS function `(t, y) => model` with an optional `float` twin for previews.

### Boundary value problems

| call | returns | notes |

| bvp({ f, interval, left, right, digits = 8, vars, time, params, guess, order }) | R BVPSolution | f is y″ as a formula in x, y and dy; each end gives { y } or { dy }. Solved by certified shooting |

| s.at(x), s.slopeAt(x) | RationalInterval | enclosures of y(x) and y′(x) |

| s.start, s.unknown, s.linear, s.unique, s.tube | | the left-end value that was solved for and which one it is; unique is proven for linear problems; tube is the ODESolution |

### Several variables

| call | returns | notes |

| field(text, ["x", "y"], { params }) | ScalarField | any number of variables |

| F.partial("x", "y"), F.gradient(), F.hessian(), F.laplacian() | ScalarFields | symbolic and simplified |

| F.jet(point, { digits, order }) | { value, gradient, hessian, smooth } | certified at a point or over a box (sides may be [a, b]) |

| F.value(point), F.directional(point, direction, { unit }) | R RationalInterval | |

| F.linearization(point) | ScalarField | the tangent plane |

| F.along({ x: "cos(t)", y: "sin(t)" }) | AnalyticFunction | the field along a curve; F.substitute fixes some variables |

| F.range(region, { digits }) | R RationalInterval | |

| F.integral(region, { digits, maxBoxes }) | R RationalInterval | product Simpson or Boole rules with proven error terms, refined where the enclosure is widest |

| F.criticalPoints(box, { digits }) | R records | { kind: min \| max \| saddle \| degenerate \| possible, unique, point, value }; a box with no record holds no critical point |

| divergence(F, vars), curl(F, vars), jacobian(F, vars) | ScalarFields | F is a list of formulas |

| lineIntegral(F, vars, curve, [t0, t1]) | R RationalInterval | ∫ F·dr for a list, ∫ f ds for one formula |

| surfaceIntegral(F, vars, surface, ["u", "v"], region) | R RationalInterval | the flux for a list, ∫∫ f dS for one formula |

A region is a box `{ x: [0, 1], y: [0, 2] }`, iterated bounds `{ x: [0, 1], y: ["0", "x^2"] }`, region text such as `"0:x:1 && 0:y:x"`, or a Core `MultiRegion` (`R.region`).

### Fourier series

| call | returns | notes |

| fourier(f, [a, b], { terms = 10, digits = 10, kind }) | R FourierSeries | f is a formula, a function or a piecewise function; kind is "full", "sine" or "cosine" (half-range) |

| S.a, S.b, S.coefficient(n), S.amplitude(n) | RationalIntervals | a[0] is a₀, so the mean is a₀/2 |

| S.partial(N) | AnalyticFunction | the partial sum, for plotting |

| S.value(x, N) | RationalInterval | the partial sum at a point |

| S.meanSquare(), S.meanSquareError(N) | RationalInterval | (1/L)∫f² and (1/L)∫(f − SN)², by Parseval |

### Sequences and series

| call | returns | notes |

| sequence(term, { variable = "n", from = 1 }) | Sequence | term(n), terms(count), limit(), monotone(), bounds(), limsup(), liminf(), accumulation(), supremum(), infimum(), nFor(ε), series(). n! is read as a factorial. See Sequences |

| deltaFor(f, x0, ε, { delta }), verifyCertificate(certificate) | { delta, largest, reason, certificate }; { valid, checks } | A δ for ε with its proof, and the independent recheck of an nFor or deltaFor certificate. See ε, N and δ |

| recursive(next, { start, variable = "x" }) | RecursiveSequence | terms(count), fixedPoints([a, b]), limit([a, b]) proven by contraction |

| sum(term, { variable = "n", from = 1 }) | Series | partial(N); divergenceTest, ratioTest, rootTest, comparisonTest, integralTest, alternatingTest, tests(); convergence(); termsForError(ε) for alternating series; sum({ digits }) with a proven tail. See Series and convergence tests |

| powerSeries(coefficient, { index = "n", from = 0, centre = 0 }) | PowerSeries | radius(), interval() with both ends examined, partial(N), at(x), value(x), derivative(), integral(). See Power series |

| taylorRemainder(f, { about, order, on }) | { coefficients, M, radius, bound, actual, holds } | Lagrange's bound beside the true maximum error |

| functionSequence(term, { variable = "x", index = "n" }) | FunctionSequence | member(n), pointwise(x), supDistance(n, [a, b], limit), uniform([a, b], limit) |

### Theorems of vector calculus

| call | returns | notes |

| greens([P, Q], [x, y], region, { flux }) | { statement, left, right, agree, overlap } | both sides enclosed; the boundary is built from the region. See Green, Stokes and the divergence theorem |

| stokes(F, vars, surface, [u, v], region) | the same shape | circulation around the image of the parameter region's boundary against the flux of the curl |

| divergenceTheorem(F, vars, solid, { surface }) | the same shape | flux through top, bottom and walls against the triple integral of the divergence |

| changeOfVariables(f, vars, map, newVars, region, { original }) | { jacobian, determinant, sign, factor, integrand, value } | See Change of variables, potentials, multipliers |

| potential(F, vars) | { conservative, curl, witness, potential, check, value } | conservative is true, false or null |

| lagrange(f, g, vars, box, { multiplier }) | { lagrangian, candidates, max, min, complete } | candidates are certified critical points of f − λg |

### Differential equations: methods

| call | returns | notes |

| firstOrder(rhs, { x, y, method }) | { type, types, steps, general, implicit, singular, through(x0, y0) } | linear, separable, Bernoulli, homogeneous. See First-order equations |

| exactEquation(M, N) | the same with { exact, factor, potential } | integrating factors in x alone or y alone |

| linearODE(coefficients, forcing) | { characteristic, roots, basis, particular, method, general, initial(values, x0) } | See Linear equations and Laplace transforms |

| laplace(f), inverseLaplace(F) | formula; { partialFractions, result } | with heaviside(t - c) and dirac(t - c); see Steps and impulses |

| laplaceSolve(coefficients, forcing, initial) | { transform, solution, pieces, verified, steps, at(t) } | See Steps and impulses |

| linearSystem(A) | { eigenvalues, kind, stability, exponential, solution(x0) } | Any size; kinds for 2 by 2. See Systems in the plane |

| planarSystem([f, g], [x, y]) | PlanarSystem | equilibria(box), jacobian(), nullclines(), conserves(H), along(V), orbit({ from, until }) |

| seriesSolution({ p, q, about, order }) | { kind, indicial, exponents, solutions, notes, radius, provenRadius }; each solution has remainder(ρ) and enclose(x) with a proven bound | See Series solutions |

| heat, laplaceRectangle, laplaceDisc | series solutions with at(…) → { value, partial, tail } | See Heat, waves and potentials |

| transport({ speed, decay, source, initial, interval }) | { kind, characteristics, foot, formula, crossing, at(x, t), residual(x, t) } | u_t + c·u_x + k·u = s by characteristics. See First-order equations: characteristics |

| wave({ c, length, position, velocity }) | { at(x, t), travelling, modes(N) } | d'Alembert's formula |

| classifyPDE({ A, B, C }), pde.classify | object | hyperbolic, parabolic or elliptic from B² − 4AC, with the region of each type when the coefficients vary |

| sturmLiouville({ p, q, w, interval, count }) | [{ index, eigenvalue, proven }] | shooting, each eigenvalue bracketed by validated solutions |

| antiderivative(tree, name), partialFractions(N, D) | | the integrals and partial fractions the methods use |

### Differential geometry

| call | returns | notes |

| curve(components, parameter, { params }) | Curve | speed(), curvature(), torsion(), evolute(), length([a, b]), totalCurvature([a, b]), at(t). See Curves |

| surface(components, [u, v], { params }) | Surface | first(), second(), normal(), gaussian(), mean(), at(u, v), area(region). See Surfaces and curvature |

| metric({ E, F, G }, [u, v]) | Metric | christoffel(), gaussian(), geodesic({ from, direction, until }), transport(path, [a, b], vector), geodesicCurvature(path, t), gaussBonnet(region). See Geodesics and Gauss-Bonnet |

| tidy(tree) | formula tree | quotient of polynomials in variables and calls, with sin² + cos² = 1 used and common factors cancelled |

| ode.solve({ …, track: false }) | | skips tracking the initial value, which is faster for a single starting point over a short span |

### Fourier transforms

| call | returns | notes |

| fourierTransform(f, { convention, support }) | FourierTransform | at(ω) as { re, im } enclosures, formula for the standard pairs (checked against the integrals), check(ω), parseval(), inversion(x). See The Fourier transform |

| inverseFourier(F).at(x) | { re, im } | from a formula for F |

| convolution(f, g) | object | at(x) enclosed; theorem(x) checks it against the product of the transforms |

| heatLine({ k, initial }) | object | the heat equation on the whole line: at(x, t), viaTransform(x, t), check(x, t), heat() |

| dft(values), fft(values) | object | exact in the field of n-th roots of unity; fft counts its multiplications and compares with the definition. See The discrete Fourier transform |

| rootOfUnity(n, k), cyclotomic(n), Cyclotomic | | exact numbers built from roots of unity |

| alias(frequency, rate), sinusoidSamples(spec), sample(f, spec) | | the alias frequency, exact samples of a sinusoid, enclosed samples of a formula |

### Numerical methods, with their true errors

| call | returns | notes |

| floatParts(x, typed?) | object | sign, exponent, mantissa, bits, the exact rational the double is, its ulp and neighbours; with the typed decimal, the exact representation error. See Floating point, exactly |

| exactOf(x), nearestDouble(q), floatOp(op, a, b) | | a double as a rational, the double nearest a rational, and one operation with the rounding it added |

| roundoff(formula, inputs) | object | the calculation in doubles and exactly, digitsLost, and steps showing where the digits go |

| bisection(f, [a, b]), newton(f, x0), secant(f, x0, x1), fixedPoint(g, x0) | object | iterations each with its true error against the certified root, and the observed order; newton(f, x0, { exact: true }) iterates in exact fractions. See Root-finding methods |

| gradientDescent(f, start, { method, step, steps }) | object | a simulated run with fixed steps, backtracking or the exact line search for quadratics; exact fractions for polynomial objectives. See Gradient descent |

| interpolate(points) or interpolate(f, { nodes }) | object | divided differences, newton, lagrange, polynomial, at(x), error(x), maxError([a, b]). See Interpolation and approximation |

| equallySpaced(a, b, n), chebyshevNodes(a, b, n) | Rational[] | nodes; the Chebyshev ones rounded to short rationals |

| spline(points), leastSquares(points, degree) | object | the natural cubic spline and the least-squares polynomial, exact |

| differences(f, x, { kind, steps }), richardson(f, x) | object | difference quotients in doubles with true error and truncation term; the extrapolation table. See Differences and quadrature rules |

| quadratureRule(f, [a, b], { rule, n }), romberg(f, [a, b]), gaussRule(f, [a, b], n) | object | the rule's value, the certified integral, the true error and the textbook bound |

| darboux(f, partition) | object | lower and upper sums, exact where f is proven monotone on each piece, else enclosures; with the certified integral between them |

| legendre(n), gaussLegendre(n) | | exact Legendre coefficients; certified nodes and weights |

| odeMethod(f, { method, t0, y0, until, steps }), stepSizeStudy(f, { …, counts }), stability(method) | object | Euler, Heun, midpoint, RK4 and Adams-Bashforth with the true global error at every step, observed order, and the stability interval. See Euler to Runge-Kutta |

### Taylor models

| call | notes |

| Domain(R`a:b`, { centre }) | centre defaults to the midpoint |

| TM.x(D, { order = 12, bits = 96 }), TM.constant(D, v), TM.polynomial(D, [a0, a1, …]) | sources |

| .add .subtract .negate .multiply .divide .pow(n) | with models or numbers |

| exp sin cos tan log log1p atan asin acos sqrt cbrt erf sinh cosh tanh reciprocal power(g, a) | elementary functions of models |

| .at(x) .range() .integral(a, b) .integrate() .derivative() | derivative only for exact polynomials |

| .coefficients .remainder .centre .order .describe() .toJSON() | |

| series(D, { coefficient or coefficients, degree, order, centre, rule, M, q, error, lookahead }) | user series; rules lagrange, ratio, alternating, explicit |

### Fast, then certified

| call | notes |

| job.quick | { value, trust }, trust is good, rough or unsure; computed on first read |

| job.stages() | generator: the preview, progress ticks { done, of, step, partial }, then the exact stage { value, via } |

| job.exact(), job.exactStage() | run to the end synchronously; the value, or the whole stage with its via line |

| await job.settle({ signal, sliceMs = 8, onStage, onProgress }) | run in time slices without blocking a page; abort with an AbortController |

| job.settled | true once the exact answer is cached |

| live(compute, onStage, { idleMs = 30, sliceMs, onProgress, onError }) | returns update(...args): each call cancels the last job, shows its preview at once and its exact answer after idleMs of quiet |

### Errors

Every refusal is an `AnalyticError` with a `code`. The common ones:

| code | when |

| domain | log, sqrt or a power is applied outside its domain (log of a range that reaches 0) |

| division-by-zero | a divisor's range contains 0 |

| not-smooth | abs, min or max at a corner inside the domain |

| overflow | exp of an argument above 2¹⁶, or a value too large to enclose |

| hypothesis | a series rule fails on the checked terms |

| outside-domain | a model or ODE solution asked about a point outside where it is valid |

| unbound | a name in a formula has no value |

| bad-expression, bad-region, bad-piecewise, bad-ode, bad-series | input that does not parse or does not make sense |

| budget | a series or search ran past its limit |

### Points, constants, plumbing

| call | notes |

| enclose.exp(x, bits) (also log, sqrt, cbrt, atan, asin, acos, sin, cos, tan, sinh, cosh, tanh, erf, log1p) | points or intervals → RationalInterval |

| constants.pi(bits), constants.e(bits) | |

| createScope({ digits, bits, order }) | callable set for evaluators: exp, sin, …, model, integral, range, fn, d, ode, zeros, … |

| Refinement, live(compute, onStage, { idleMs }) | the shared fast-then-exact shape |

| parse, format, differentiate(ast, name), compileFloat(ast), modelOf(ast, env, base), encloseAst(ast, env, bits), freeVariables(ast) | expression tools |

| num(v), v(name), op(o, ...args), call(name, ...args) | build an AST by hand |

| parsePiecewiseText(text) | [[region, rule], …] or null when the text is not piecewise |

### Try it

```js
// Look something up in the tables above and try it here.
const f = fn("x^2*exp(-x)");
PRINT("f(1) =", f.value(1, { digits: 15 }).exact());
PRINT("f' =", f.derivative().toString());
f.range(R`0:5`, { digits: 6 }).exact()
```
